When you pass `--mcp-config` explicitly, the wait has a longer deadline; see that flag's entry for the cached-server exception

env_var:MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS.description: How long blocking MCP startup waits, in milliseconds, for the connection batch before snapshotting the tool list (default: 5000). Applies when `MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=0` or for servers marked `alwaysLoad: true`. Servers still pending at the deadline keep connecting in the background but won't appear until the next query. Distinct from `MCP_TIMEOUT`, which bounds an individual server's connect attempt

How long blocking MCP startup waits, in milliseconds, for the connection batch before snapshotting the tool list (default: 5000). Applies when `MCP_CONNECTION_NONBLOCKING=0` or for servers marked `alwaysLoad: true`. Servers still pending at the deadline keep connecting in the background. Distinct from `MCP_TIMEOUT`, which bounds an individual server's connect attempt

env_var:MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE.description: Set to `0` to turn off the cross-process MCP discovery cache, so every server connects at startup instead of showing the `connects on first use` cached status and connecting on its first tool call. The cached status requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

Turns the MCP discovery cache on or off. With the cache on, a remote HTTP or SSE server you've used before can show the `cached` status, and Claude Code connects it on its first tool call instead of at startup. The cache is off by default unless a gradual rollout has enabled it for your account. Set to `1` to turn it on, or `0` to keep it off even when the rollout has enabled it. Before v2.1.238, the cache was on by default. The `cached` status requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

env_var:MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_MAX_STALE_S.description: Maximum age, in seconds, of a discovery-cache entry (default: 14400, or 4 hours). At a start where the entry is older than that, Claude Code discards it and connects the server at startup, as it does with the cache off. Claude Code caps the value at 7 days. Before v2.1.238, the default was 86400, or 24 hours, and Claude Code didn't cap the value

env_var:MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_STRIKES.description: At a start where a discovery-cache entry is older than `MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_S`, Claude Code refreshes it in the background. This variable sets how many refreshes in a row can fail before Claude Code discards the entry and connects the server at the next start instead (default: 1). Raise it if your network connection drops occasionally, so that one failed refresh doesn't discard the entry. Requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later

env_var:MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_S.description: Seconds for which Claude Code uses a discovery-cache entry without refreshing it (default: 900). At a start where the entry is older than that, Claude Code still uses it but refreshes it in the background. Once the entry is older than `MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_MAX_STALE_S`, Claude Code discards it instead. Claude Code caps the value at `MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE_MAX_STALE_S`, which is 4 hours by default. Before v2.1.238, Claude Code didn't cap the value

env_var:MCP_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT.description: Fixed port for the OAuth redirect callback, as an alternative to `--callback-port` when adding an MCP server with pre-configured credentials

env_var:MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION.description: On the v2 MCP client runtime only, whether Claude Code probes servers for MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28. Set `auto` to probe HTTP, claude.ai connector, and stdio servers; a server that doesn't answer the probe connects on the earlier protocol instead, as SSE and WebSocket servers always do. Set `legacy` to skip the probe for every server. Without the variable, Claude Code probes HTTP and claude.ai connector servers on Claude Code v2.1.232 or later, with the exceptions the MCP client runtimes section lists. Any other value is ignored with a warning in the debug log. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

On the v2 MCP client runtime only, whether Claude Code probes servers for MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28. Set `auto` to probe HTTP, claude.ai connector, and stdio servers; a server that doesn't answer the probe connects on the earlier protocol instead, as SSE and WebSocket servers always do. Set `legacy` to skip the probe for every server. Without the variable, Claude Code probes HTTP servers, and also probes claude.ai connector servers in sessions where it fetches feature flags. Any other value is ignored with a warning in the debug log. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

On the v2 MCP client runtime only, whether Claude Code probes servers for MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28. Set `auto` to probe HTTP, claude.ai connector, and stdio servers, or `legacy` to probe none. With the variable unset, Claude Code probes the servers described under MCP client runtimes. Any other value is ignored with a warning in the debug log. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

On the v2 MCP client runtime only, controls whether Claude Code probes servers for MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28. Set `legacy` to skip the probe, so that every server connects with the handshake from before that revision. Set `auto` to probe the server kinds that support the probe: HTTP and stdio servers, claude.ai connectors, and the connectors of cloud and Remote Control sessions. With the variable unset, Claude Code probes those same kinds by default; see MCP client runtimes. Any other value is ignored with a warning in the debug log. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

On the v2 MCP client runtime only, controls whether Claude Code probes servers for MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28. Set `legacy` to keep every server on the earlier handshake, or `auto` to probe the server kinds that support it. Unset, Claude Code probes them but can skip some servers. Any other value is ignored with a warning in the debug log. Requires Claude Code v2.1.221 or later

env_var:MCP_REMOTE_SERVER_CONNECTION_BAT.description: Maximum number of remote MCP servers (HTTP/SSE) to connect in parallel during startup (default: 20)

env_var:MCP_SDK_GENERATION.description: Pin which MCP client runtime this process uses, the implementation behind MCP server connections, while Claude Code migrates from its v1 runtime to v2. Set `v1` to stay on the current runtime or `v2` to opt in early. Without the variable, a gradual rollout decides, and defaults to v1. On Claude Code v2.1.221 or later, the v2 runtime checks the issuer an MCP OAuth server returns in its authorization response and fails the sign-in with an error that begins `Issuer mismatch in authorization response` when it doesn't match. The v1 runtime doesn't run this check. If you set an unrecognized value, Claude Code ignores it and writes a warning to the debug log. Claude Code reads the value once per process. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later

Pin which MCP client runtime this process connects to MCP servers with: `v1`, built on MCP TypeScript SDK 1.x, or `v2`, built on MCP TypeScript SDK 2.0. Without the variable, Claude Code uses v2 on Claude Code v2.1.232 or later, except where that section says it uses v1. On Claude Code v2.1.221 or later, the v2 runtime checks the issuer an MCP OAuth server returns in its authorization response and fails the sign-in with an error that begins `Issuer mismatch in authorization response` when it doesn't match. The v1 runtime doesn't run this check. If you set an unrecognized value, Claude Code ignores it and writes a warning to the debug log. Claude Code reads the value once per process. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later

Pin which MCP client runtime this process connects to MCP servers with: `v1`, built on MCP TypeScript SDK 1.x, or `v2`, built on MCP TypeScript SDK 2.0. Without the variable, Claude Code uses v2, starting with the versions listed in that section. On Claude Code v2.1.221 or later, the v2 runtime checks the issuer an MCP OAuth server returns in its authorization response and fails the sign-in with an error that begins `Issuer mismatch in authorization response` when it doesn't match. The v1 runtime doesn't run this check. If you set an unrecognized value, Claude Code ignores it and writes a warning to the debug log. Claude Code reads the value once per process. Requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later

env_var:MCP_SERVER_CONNECTION_BATCH_SIZE.description: Maximum number of local MCP servers (stdio) to connect in parallel during startup (default: 3)

env_var:MCP_TIMEOUT.description: Timeout in milliseconds for MCP server startup (default: 30000, or 30 seconds)

env_var:MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT.description: Timeout in milliseconds for MCP tool execution (default: 100000000, about 28 hours). A per-server `timeout` field in `.mcp.json` overrides this for that server. For the env variable, values below 1000 are floored to one second; for the per-server field, values below 1000 are ignored

Timeout in milliseconds for MCP tool execution (default: 100000000, about 28 hours). A per-server `timeout` field in `.mcp.json` overrides this for that server. A per-server `timeout` of at least 1000 also sets the minimum idle window for that server's tool calls, so `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` never aborts them sooner; this floor requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. For the env variable, values below 1000 are floored to one second; for the per-server field, values below 1000 are ignored

Timeout in milliseconds for MCP tool execution (default: 100000000, about 28 hours). For an HTTP, SSE, or claude.ai connector server, each request also times out after 60 seconds by default; set this variable, or the per-server `timeout`, above 60000 to raise that per-request limit. A lower value still shortens the overall tool-execution timeout but leaves the per-request limit at 60 seconds. Stdio and WebSocket servers have no per-request timer. A per-server `timeout` field in `.mcp.json` overrides this for that server. A per-server `timeout` of at least 1000 also sets the minimum idle window for that server's tool calls, so `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` never aborts them sooner; this floor requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. For the env variable, values below 1000 are floored to one second; for the per-server field, values below 1000 are ignored

env_var:NO_PROXY.description: List of domains and IPs to which requests will be directly issued, bypassing proxy

env_var:OTEL_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMI.description: Standard OpenTelemetry SDK limit on attribute value length. Claude Code caps content-bearing telemetry attributes at the smaller of this and `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH`, so the truncation marker stays within the SDK limit. Claude Code reads the `OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT` and `OTEL_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT` variants the same way, and the smallest set value applies to all signals. Requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT.description: OTLP collector endpoint for all signals

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT.description: OTLP logs endpoint, overrides general setting

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS.description: Authentication headers for logs, merged with the general headers

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_PROTOCOL.description: Protocol for logs, overrides general setting

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPO.description: OTLP metrics endpoint, overrides general setting

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_HEADE.description: Authentication headers for metrics, merged with the general headers

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_PROTO.description: Protocol for metrics, overrides general setting

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPO.description: Metrics temporality preference (default: `delta`). Set to `cumulative` if your backend expects cumulative temporality

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL.description: Protocol for OTLP exporter, applies to all signals. Claude Code has no default protocol, so set this or the signal-specific protocol variable for each `otlp` exporter you enable

Protocol for OTLP exporter, applies to all signals. Defaults to `http/protobuf` for a valid `http://` or `https://` endpoint. For a gRPC endpoint such as `http://localhost:4317`, set this to `grpc`. The default requires Claude Code v2.1.323 or later

env_var:OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADER.description: Authentication headers for traces, merged with `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`

env_var:OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER.description: Logs/events exporter types, comma-separated. Use `none` to disable

env_var:OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES.description: Set to `1` to include the model's response text on `assistant_response` OpenTelemetry log events. When unset, the value of `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS` is used instead. Set to `0` to keep responses redacted even when `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS` is set. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later. See Monitoring

Set to `1` to include the model's response text on `assistant_response` OpenTelemetry log events. When unset, Claude Code uses the value of `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS` instead. Set to `0` to keep responses redacted even when `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS` is set. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_LOG_MANAGED_SETTINGS.description: Set to `1` to add the redacted managed settings, and a SHA-256 digest of the settings before redaction, to `managed_settings_resolved` OpenTelemetry log events. Disabled by default. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings; a value in project or local settings doesn't turn it on. Requires Claude Code v2.1.274 or later. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES.description: Emit Anthropic Messages API request and response JSON as `api_request_body` / `api_response_body` log events. Set to `1` for inline bodies truncated at 60 KB, or `file:<dir>` to write untruncated bodies to disk and emit a `body_ref` path instead. Disabled by default; bodies include the entire conversation history. See Monitoring

Emit Anthropic Messages API request and response JSON as `api_request_body` / `api_response_body` log events. Set to `1` for inline bodies truncated at the content limit, or `file:<dir>` to write untruncated bodies to disk and emit a `body_ref` path instead. `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH` configures the content limit, 60 KB by default. Disabled by default; bodies include the entire conversation history. See Monitoring

Emit Anthropic Messages API request and response JSON as `api_request_body` / `api_response_body` log events. Set to `1` for inline bodies truncated at the content limit, or `file:<dir>` to write untruncated bodies to disk and emit a `body_ref` path instead. `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH` configures the content limit, 60 KB by default. Disabled by default; bodies include the entire conversation history. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT.description: Set to `1` to include tool input and output content in OpenTelemetry span events. Disabled by default to protect sensitive data. See Monitoring

Set to `1` to include tool content in the `tool.output` OpenTelemetry span event. Span attributes carry tool content under their own gates. Requires tracing. Disabled by default to protect sensitive data. See Monitoring

Set to `1` to include tool content in the `tool.output` OpenTelemetry span event. Span attributes carry tool content under their own gates. Requires tracing. Disabled by default to protect sensitive data. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings, apart from the off values that section describes. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS.description: Set to `1` to include tool input arguments, MCP server names, raw error strings on tool failures, the refusal `category` on `api_refusal` events, and other tool details in OpenTelemetry traces and logs. Disabled by default to protect PII. See Monitoring

Set to `1` to include tool input arguments, MCP server names, user-authored workflow names, raw error strings on tool failures, the refusal `category` on `api_refusal` events, and other tool details in OpenTelemetry traces and logs. Disabled by default to protect PII. See Monitoring

Set to `1` to include tool input arguments, MCP server names, user-authored workflow names, raw error strings on tool failures, the refusal `category` on `api_refusal` events, and other tool details in OpenTelemetry traces and logs. Disabled by default to protect PII. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings, apart from the off values that section describes. See Monitoring

Set to `1` to include tool input arguments; MCP server names; user-authored workflow names; raw error strings on tool failures; the refusal `category` on `api_refusal` events; real agent, skill, plugin, and MCP server names on cost and token metrics; and other tool details in OpenTelemetry metrics, traces, and logs. Disabled by default to protect PII. Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings, apart from the off values that section describes. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS.description: Set to `1` to include user prompt text in OpenTelemetry traces and logs. Disabled by default (prompts are redacted). See Monitoring

Set to `1` to include user prompt text in OpenTelemetry traces and logs. Disabled by default (prompts are redacted). Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings, apart from the off values that section describes. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER.description: Metrics exporter types, comma-separated. Use `none` to disable

env_var:OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ACCOUNT_UUI.description: Set to `false` to exclude account UUID from metrics attributes (default: included). See Monitoring
Set to `false` to exclude account UUID from metric and event attributes (default: included). See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_ENTRYPOINT.description: Set to `true` to include the session entrypoint in metrics attributes (default: excluded). Added in v2.1.152. See Monitoring
Set to `true` to include the session entrypoint in metric and event attributes (default: excluded). Added in v2.1.152. See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_REPOSITORY.description: Set to `true` to tag OpenTelemetry metrics and events with `vcs.*` attributes identifying the session's repository (default: excluded). Requires Claude Code v2.1.269 or later. See Repository attributes

env_var:OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_RESOURCE_AT.description: As of v2.1.161, Claude Code attaches `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` keys to metric datapoint labels. Set to `false` to exclude them (default: included). See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID.description: Set to `false` to exclude session ID from metrics attributes (default: included). See Monitoring
Set to `false` to exclude session ID from metric and event attributes (default: included). See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_VERSION.description: Set to `true` to include Claude Code version in metrics attributes (default: excluded). See Monitoring
Set to `true` to include Claude Code version in metric and event attributes (default: excluded). See Monitoring

env_var:OTEL_RESOURCE_INCLUDE_HOST.description: Set to `1` to add the machine's name and ID to OpenTelemetry resource attributes as `host.name` and `host.id` (default: excluded). Set it in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Ignored in project and local settings. Requires Claude Code v2.1.326 or later. See Identify the machine a session ran on

env_var:OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER.description: Traces exporter types, comma-separated. Use `none` to disable

env_var:OTEL_TRACES_EXPORT_INTERVAL.description: Span batch export interval in milliseconds (default: 5000)

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_BASE_DIR.description: Directory for repository checkouts and per-session working directories. The runner needs write access to this path or its parent. The runner creates the directory at startup and exits with `cannot create or write to base directory` when it can't create or write to it. Before v2.1.225, the runner created the directory when the first session started, so an unusable path failed sessions rather than startup. On Windows, which isn't a supported runner host, there is no default: the runner exits at startup unless you pass the flag or set the variable. Use the same value on every runner in an environment. See Keep the base directory and capacity identical across runners.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_BG_RESULT_GRA.description: How long the runner considers a session busy after a background task finishes while the follow-up turn that reads the result hasn't started. The `--drain-wait-sec` and `--release-idle-session-min` rows describe where the hold applies on drain and idle release, and Runner lifecycle describes where it applies on `--retire-at` retirement. `0` or an unusable value falls back to the default, so the hold can't be turned off. Requires Claude Code v2.1.228 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_CLIENT_LABEL.description: Label the runner sends when it registers. The runner also reports it as the `client_label` label of `claude_code_self_hosted_runner_info`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_CONFIGURE_GIT.description: At startup, write global git identity, enable Anthropic commit signing, turn on git push negotiation, and install commit hooks that append a `Co-authored-by:` trailer. Push negotiation requires Claude Code v2.1.257 or later. See Configure git.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_CONFINE_REPO_.description: Sets the mode of the guard that flags a session when a repository's committed settings try to grant write or read access outside that session's own workspace, set environment variables, or override the operator's sandbox or hooks posture, such as `sandbox.enabled: false` or `disableAllHooks`. The default `warn` logs the violation and still starts the session, `enforce` refuses the session, and `off` disables the scan. See Harden your deployment.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_DEBUG_TOKEN_D.description: Write live tokens to disk for inspection. Debug only; don't use in production.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_DEFER_SHUTDOW.description: On the first `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, keep serving the sessions already attached instead of draining them, then release whatever is still attached N minutes later and exit. Raise your host's stop timeout before you set this. See Defer the drain past the first signal. `0` disables. Requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_DRAIN_GRACE_M.description: Until the runner receives a shutdown signal or reaches its retire time, controls when the runner exits after its active sessions finish: `0` exits immediately without polling for more, and a positive value keeps the runner alive and re-polling the locked owner's queue for that many seconds first, at the cost of the per-session container isolation described in the hardening section. After a first signal you deferred with `--defer-shutdown-max-min`, the runner exits as soon as it holds no sessions, whatever you set here.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_DRAIN_MARKER_.description: Marker file that your host writes to announce a graceful drain before sending `SIGTERM`. When the file exists as the drain starts, the runner reports its exit to Anthropic as a host drain rather than a plain shutdown signal. The drain itself, including the `--drain-wait-sec` hold, runs the same as without the flag. Name a path on a local filesystem that sessions can't write to. Requires Claude Code v2.1.271 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_DRAIN_WAIT_MS.description: Once the drain starts, which is on `SIGTERM` unless you set `--defer-shutdown-max-min`, wait up to N seconds for each session's in-flight turn and background tasks to finish before terminating the child. During this wait, the runner counts a background task that has just finished as still running until the follow-up turn that reads its result starts, for at most the `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_BG_RESULT_GRACE_MS` window.

Once the drain starts, which is on `SIGTERM` unless you set `--defer-shutdown-max-min`, wait up to N seconds for each session's in-flight turn and background tasks to finish before terminating the child. During this wait, the runner counts a background task that has just finished as still running until the follow-up turn that reads its result starts, for at most the `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_BG_RESULT_GRACE_MS` window. Raise your stop timeout too.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT_S.description: Path to a file containing the environment secret, or, for runners spawned by the orchestrator, the single-use work-order JWT. `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT_SECRET` carries the secret value directly, not a file path. The older `--pool-secret-file` flag and `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_POOL_SECRET` variable still work and print a deprecation notice to stderr; preview-program runner builds older than 2.1.216 only recognize those older names.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_EXEC_PATH.description: Binary or wrapper script to spawn for each session. See Wrapper scripts.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_HEALTH_PORT.description: Port for the `/healthz` and `/metrics` listener. Set `0` to disable.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_HOLD_IDLE_FIL.description: File your host keeps changing to hold an idle session on the runner. See Keep an idle session while its processes run. Requires Claude Code v2.1.311 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_HOOKS_DIR.description: Directory of lifecycle hook scripts. See Lifecycle hooks.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_HOST_CONFIG_D.description: Directory captured into the runner's startup snapshot and seeded into each session's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; changes on disk apply after a runner restart. Setting the variable also moves where the runner reads `.claude.json` for MCP seeding, so setting it, including to its own default, relocates that lookup; point at an empty directory to disable seeding entirely.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_HOST_CONFIG_S.description: Where the runner keeps the startup snapshot of the host config directory that it seeds each session from. `disk` copies the snapshot into a runner-owned directory under `--base-dir` and, at each session start, verifies every file against an in-memory digest. If a file in the copy has been modified, the session fails and the runner refuses sessions until you restart it. `memory` holds the whole snapshot on the heap, capped at 64 MiB; over the cap, sessions start without host config and show a notice saying so. When the runner can't write the disk snapshot, it logs the failure and uses `memory` for that run. Requires Claude Code v2.1.271 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_IDLE_SHUTDOWN.description: Exit after N minutes of polling with no work ever assigned, for autoscaler scale-down. `0` disables.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_LOCK_TO_ACCOU.description: Pre-lock the runner to a specific account at startup instead of locking on first session. Accepts an email address or `user_...` ID in the environment's organization. A pre-locked runner never picks up Claude Tag channel sessions, which have no account.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_LOG_FILE.description: Mirror runner logs to a file in addition to stdout and stderr, created with `0600` permissions. Required for `self-hosted-runner doctor` to tail logs locally.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_MAX_HOLD_MS.description: With `--hold-idle-file`, release a held session anyway N minutes after it went idle. A value at or below `--release-idle-session-min` holds nothing. `0` turns the hold off. Requires Claude Code v2.1.311 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_MAX_LIFETIME_.description: How long the runner waits after a session reaches its `--kill-session-after-min` limit, for a running turn to finish or the release to complete, before it terminates the session

Limit a session to N minutes wall-clock, as a safety limit for stuck sessions. On v2.1.260 or later, the runner releases a session that reaches the limit so it can resume on its user's next message, and terminates it only if it's still on the runner when the `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_MAX_LIFETIME_GRACE_MS` grace window ends. Before v2.1.260, the runner terminated the session at the limit. See Some sessions don't count as idle for the details and how to choose a value. `0` disables.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_POST_SESSION_.description: Budget for the `post-session` hook on every session end, including runner shutdown

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_POST_TURN_SET.description: Cap on how long the runner counts a session as busy for the `--drain-wait-sec` drain after a turn finishes, while the session's process reports the turn's end to Anthropic. `0` or an unusable value falls back to the default, so the hold can't be turned off. Requires Claude Code v2.1.275 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_PROXY_AUTHORI.description: Shell command the runner runs for every connection to your egress proxy, using its trimmed stdout as the `Proxy-Authorization` header value. Requires `HTTPS_PROXY` or `HTTP_PROXY`, and can't be combined with `--proxy-authorization-file`. See Authenticate to an egress proxy. Requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later.

File the runner reads for every connection to your egress proxy, using its trimmed contents as the `Proxy-Authorization` header value. Use this flag for a token another process rotates in place. Carries the same requirements as `--proxy-authorization-command`, and can't be combined with it. See Authenticate to an egress proxy. Requires Claude Code v2.1.238 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_PUSH_OUTCOME_.description: On a runner-initiated session end such as a drain or idle release, push tracked outcome branches to `origin` before deleting the workspace, so in-flight commits survive a restart. Best-effort; adds 30 seconds to the shutdown budget, and requires git 2.29 or newer to resume from the pushed branch. Restrict push access to `claude/*` refs before enabling; see Resumed sessions lose unpushed work. Repositories checked out via a `checkout` lifecycle hook aren't pushed; snapshot those from the `post-session` hook instead.

On a runner-initiated session end such as a drain or idle release, the runner pushes primary session branches with new commits to `origin` before deleting the workspace. Best-effort; adds 30 seconds to the shutdown budget. Requires git 2.29 or later to resume from them. Restrict push access to `claude/*` refs; see Resumed sessions lose unpushed work. A `checkout` hook's repositories aren't pushed; snapshot those from the `post-session` hook.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_REMOVE_SESSIO.description: Remove a session's per-session directories under `<base-dir>/_sessions/` when the session ends on this runner, whatever the outcome. Reuse a pre-warmed checkout describes what they hold and who can read them when they stay. The removal is best-effort: the per-session directories stay in place when the runner is killed or reaches its drain deadline before cleanup runs. With the flag on, a failed or interrupted session's debug log isn't kept on disk. Requires Claude Code v2.1.268 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_REPOSITORY_FO.description: At `--capacity 1`, use `<folder>` as the clone of a repository that no `checkout` hook prepares. Repeatable; comma-separated in the variable. See Reuse a pre-warmed checkout. Requires Claude Code v2.1.328 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_RETIRE_AT.description: Retire the runner at an absolute Unix timestamp in seconds, for infrastructure that kills the runner at a known time; Runner lifecycle describes the release sequence and how to size the margin. Values before 2001 or after the year 5138 are rejected by the flag and ignored by the environment variable.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_SERVER_AUTO_M.description: Which of the auto mode classifier rule lists that the control plane sends with a session may reach that session: `all`, `no-allow`, or `none`. See Auto mode rule lists for what each value applies. An invalid value stops the runner at startup. Requires Claude Code v2.1.295 or later.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_SESSION_IDLE_.description: Release a session slot after N minutes of inactivity once a turn finishes or the session waits for the user's action. A session that's still mid-turn, including one holding a never-finishing background task or an approval requested from inside a running tool call, doesn't count as idle; pair with `--kill-session-after-min` as the hard backstop. After a session's background task finishes, the runner considers the session busy until the follow-up turn that reads the result starts, for at most the `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_BG_RESULT_GRACE_MS` window. Until the runner receives a shutdown signal or reaches its retire time, a release that leaves the runner with no active sessions starts the same exit path as a normal drain, governed by `--drain-grace-sec`. After a first signal you deferred with `--defer-shutdown-max-min`, the runner exits as soon as a release leaves it holding no sessions. `0` disables.

Release a session slot after N minutes of inactivity once a turn finishes or the session waits for the user's action. Some sessions don't count as idle, so pair with `--kill-session-after-min`. A finished background task keeps the session busy for at most the `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_BG_RESULT_GRACE_MS` window. To delay a release, set `--hold-idle-file`. `0` disables.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_SESSION_STOP_.description: How long to wait for the Claude process to exit cleanly after a session ends, before force-killing it. Raise the value if the child's own `SessionEnd` hooks need more time.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GRACE.description: How long the runner waits for the OS to deliver `SIGKILL` to a child stuck in uninterruptible I/O before exiting itself. Floored at `--post-session-hook-timeout-sec` plus 15 seconds, and 30 more when `--push-outcome-on-release` is set, so the effective minimum is 75 seconds at defaults.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_STARTUP_TIMEO.description: Release a session slot if the child hasn't signaled on the activity channel that it initialized within N minutes. The N minutes start at spawn, after cloning, and start over at each `user` or `assistant` message the child emits before it has initialized or reported its state. Before v2.1.299, this timeout stopped applying at the session's first such message. For release after the init signal, see `--release-idle-session-min`. `0` disables.

How long to wait on a child process that hasn't initialized before releasing the session's slot. See Session startup timeout for where the count starts and which sessions it leaves running. `0` disables the timeout.

env_var:SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_TRUST_WORKSPA.description: Seed persisted trust for each session's repository paths so repo-committed `permissions.allow` and `additionalDirectories` are honored. Set `false` to drop repo-committed permission grants and configure allow rules in the host config's `settings.json` instead; repository-committed `sandbox.*` settings still apply either way, which is why the repo-settings guard scans them regardless of this flag.

env_var:SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET.description: Override the character budget for skill metadata shown to the Skill tool. The budget scales dynamically at 1% of the context window, with a fallback of 8,000 characters. Legacy name kept for backwards compatibility

env_var:TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH.description: Maximum number of characters in subagent output before truncation (default: 32000, maximum: 160000). When truncated, the full output is saved to disk and the path is included in the truncated response

Maximum number of characters of a background task's output that the `TaskOutput` tool keeps (default: 32000; maximum: 160000). If you set the `taskOutputMaxChars` setting, Claude Code ignores this variable

Removed in v2.1.277 and now a no-op, together with the `TaskOutput` tool it sized. Previously set the maximum number of characters of a background task's output that the `TaskOutput` tool kept. Claude reads a background task's output file with `Read` instead

hook_event:ConfigChange.description: When a configuration file changes during a session

hook_event:CwdChanged.description: When the working directory changes, for example when Claude executes a `cd` command. Useful for reactive environment management with tools like direnv

hook_event:DirectoryAdded.description: When a working directory is added mid-session via `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request

hook_event:Elicitation.description: When an MCP server requests user input during a tool call

hook_event:ElicitationResult.description: After a user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server

hook_event:FileChanged.description: When a watched file changes on disk. The `matcher` field specifies which filenames to watch

hook_event:InstructionsLoaded.description: When a CLAUDE.md or `.claude/rules/*.md` file is loaded into context. Fires at session start and when files are lazily loaded during a session

hook_event:MessageDisplay.description: While assistant message text is displayed

hook_event:Notification.description: When Claude Code sends a notification

hook_event:PermissionDenied.description: When auto mode denies a tool call, including denials without a classifier verdict. Use JSON `hookSpecificOutput.retry: true` to tell the model it may retry the denied tool call. Claude Code ignores `retry` when the classifier produced no verdict

hook_event:PermissionRequest.description: When a tool call needs a permission decision

hook_event:PostModelSwitch.description: After the session's model changes, including changes Claude Code makes on its own, such as restoring the model when you resume a session

hook_event:PostToolBatch.description: After a full batch of parallel tool calls resolves, before the next model call

hook_event:PreModelSwitch.description: Before Claude Code applies a model switch that you or a client requested. Can block the switch

hook_event:PreToolUse.description: Before a tool call executes. Can block it

hook_event:SessionStart.description: When a session begins or resumes

hook_event:Setup.description: When you start Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in `-p` mode. For one-time preparation in CI or scripts

hook_event:StopFailure.description: When the turn ends due to an API error

hook_event:TaskCompleted.description: When a task is being marked as completed

hook_event:TaskCreated.description: When a task is being created via `TaskCreate`

hook_event:TeammateIdle.description: When an agent team teammate is about to go idle

hook_event:UserPromptExpansion.description: When a user-typed command expands into a prompt, before it reaches Claude. Can block the expansion

hook_event:UserPromptSubmit.description: When a prompt is submitted, before Claude processes it. Also fires on turns Claude Code starts on its own

hook_event:WorktreeCreate.description: When a worktree is being created via `--worktree`, `isolation: "worktree"`, or for a background session. Replaces default git behavior

hook_event:WorktreeRemove.description: When a worktree that a `WorktreeCreate` hook created is being removed

mod_event:agent.offer.description: A subagent type is offered to Claude

mod_event:agent.spawn.description: A subagent or an agent team teammate is about to start. For a teammate, `e.isTeammate` is `true`.
A subagent or an agent team teammate is about to start, or a subagent that finished or stopped is about to run again. For a teammate, `e.isTeammate` is `true`. For a resumed run, `e.resume` is set.

mod_event:attribution.text.description: Claude Code composes commit or pull request attribution text

mod_event:command.describe.description: Once for each command, for the command list

mod_event:command.run.description: A command is about to run

mod_event:config.set.description: A `/config` row is about to change

mod_event:engine.create.description: The mods API is being built for this mod

mod_event:plugin.register.description: A hooks module is about to load. `e.uses` lists its events, mods API calls, environment variables, and state, as `claude plugin validate` prints them. Each call is written without the `$.` prefix, such as `fs.read`.

A hooks module is about to load, or, on v2.1.326 or later, a plugin without one. `e.uses` lists the module's events, mods API calls, environment variables, and state, as `claude plugin validate` prints them. Each call is written without the `$.` prefix, such as `fs.read`.

mod_event:prompt.attachment.description: Claude Code adds a message of its own for Claude, such as a reminder. `e.type` names the kind, and for the kinds the types declare, `e.detail` holds the facts the text was written from.

mod_event:prompt.autocomplete.description: The user types in the prompt box and a word ends at the cursor. `e.token` is that word. Claude Code doesn't wait for the hook: its own autocomplete rows show first.

mod_event:prompt.compose.description: Claude Code renders a system prompt

mod_event:prompt.context.description: Once for each conversation, for the context sent with the first message

mod_event:prompt.edit.description: The user edits the prompt box

mod_event:prompt.fill.description: Text is about to go into the prompt box as a draft, or as a dim suggestion

mod_event:prompt.mention.description: Claude Code is about to read a file that a prompt @-mentions. Requires Claude Code v2.1.290 or later.

mod_event:prompt.section.description: Once for each named section of the system prompt. `e.name` is the section's `id` in `prompt.compose`.

mod_event:prompt.suggest.description: Text is about to go into the prompt box as a draft, or as a dim suggestion

mod_event:session.append.description: Once for each row the conversation keeps, such as a prompt, a response block, a tool result, or a notice, before it's stored

mod_event:session.attach.description: Another app connects to or disconnects from the session

mod_event:session.compact.description: The conversation is about to be compacted

mod_event:session.detach.description: Another app connects to or disconnects from the session

mod_event:session.end.description: The session ends, or `/clear`, `/resume`, or `/branch` runs. `e.reason` is `clear`, `resume`, `logout`, `prompt_input_exit`, or `other`. `/branch` reports `resume`.

mod_event:session.measure.description: After each turn, and when a plan limit's percent used changes

mod_event:session.receive.description: A message arrives from, or is about to go to, another agent or session. See Send and receive messages between sessions.

mod_event:session.send.description: A message arrives from, or is about to go to, another agent or session. See Send and receive messages between sessions.

mod_event:session.start.description: Once for each loaded mod, before the first prompt, and again after a reload of that mod. Not after `/clear`, `/resume`, or `/branch`.

mod_event:session.stop.description: The user stops Claude, such as with Esc during a turn. Requires Claude Code v2.1.326 or later.

mod_event:settings.read.description: A mod calls `$.settings.read`, or Claude Code builds the session's merged settings
A mod calls `$.settings.read`, or Claude Code builds the session's merged settings. Requires Claude Code v2.1.304 or later on Claude Code's own read and for `e.layers`

mod_event:skill.prompt.description: A skill's text is expanded for Claude

mod_event:telemetry.log.description: A telemetry record is about to be logged, or one use of a feature is marked. In a mod you install, give a telemetry hook the filter `{ to: 'collector' }`, as in `on('telemetry.log', { to: 'collector' }, hook)`. Without the filter, the mod fails `claude plugin validate`. `*` doesn't match these events.

mod_event:telemetry.mark.description: A telemetry record is about to be logged, or one use of a feature is marked. In a mod you install, give a telemetry hook the filter `{ to: 'collector' }`, as in `on('telemetry.log', { to: 'collector' }, hook)`. Without the filter, the mod fails `claude plugin validate`. `*` doesn't match these events.

mod_event:tool.call.description: A tool is about to run

mod_event:tool.check.description: Claude Code decides whether a tool call may run, after the `tool.call` and `PreToolUse` hooks. `next(e)` resolves to the decision the rules, the permission mode, and those hooks reached.

mod_event:tool.describe.description: Once for each tool, when its description is first sent to Claude. A second time for an MCP tool when Claude loads it through tool search, with `e.description` set to the text Claude reads for the loaded tool.

mod_event:tool.judge.description: Auto mode is about to ask its classifier about a call. Requires Claude Code v2.1.326 or later.

mod_event:tool.run.description: An allowed call is about to run. Requires Claude Code v2.1.326 or later.

mod_event:turn.step.description: One request is about to go to the model

mod_event:ui.close.description: A pane is about to close. `e.id` is the pane and `e.origin.kind` is `plugin`, `person`, or `unload`.

mod_event:ui.fault.description: A `Client` element your mod drew failed to load, draw, or run. `e.phase` is `load`, `render`, or `run`, and `e.reason` is the error message. Requires Claude Code v2.1.289 or later.

mod_event:ui.focus.description: The focused control or the scroll position of a pane or the band is about to change

mod_event:ui.input.description: A `Button`, `Input`, or `Select` a mod drew is used

mod_event:ui.message.description: A `Client` element posts data to its mod

mod_event:ui.press.description: A `Button`, `Input`, or `Select` a mod drew is used

mod_event:ui.render.description: A render site is about to be drawn

mod_event:ui.resolve.description: Mods load, once for each app, render site, and mod. The result is the element table that `$.ui.resolve(e)` reads.

mod_event:ui.scroll.description: The focused control or the scroll position of a pane or the band is about to change

mod_event:ui.select.description: A `Button`, `Input`, or `Select` a mod drew is used
